name: Proxmox Daily Log Summary with hardware stats -Groq

parameters.text:
=Log excerpt {{ $json.chunkIndex }}/{{ $json.totalChunks }} from a Proxmox host, covering {{ $json.dateLabel }}. Analyze and extract notable events only, following the rules in your instructions:

{{ $json.text }}

messageValues.message:
You are a Proxmox VE system log analyst. You will be given a raw excerpt of syslog/journal entries from a Proxmox host. Your only job is to extract genuinely notable events from this excerpt — nothing else.

Flag only:
- Errors, failures, crashes, panics
- Security-relevant events: authentication failures, unauthorized access attempts, firewall denials
- Resource issues: disk full/near-full, ZFS pool degraded/corrupt, OOM killer, high load, memory pressure
- Hardware warnings: disk SMART errors, network interface flapping, thermal issues
- Mail delivery failures: bounced, blocked, deferred or rejected outbound mail, SPF/DKIM authentication failures
- CPU issues: soft lockups, hung tasks, machine check exceptions, thermal throttling
- Backup/replication failures
- Anything else clearly abnormal for a healthy running system

Ignore routine, expected chatter: normal service start/stop messages, routine cron/systemd timer ticks, pvestatd/pvedaemon polling, normal DHCP renewals, and anything that is just informational status with no problem indicated.

Output format: one line per notable event, formatted as:
[TIME] SEVERITY: short description

If this excerpt contains no notable events, output exactly: NONE

Do not summarize the whole excerpt. Do not add commentary. Do not repeat identical events more than once — if you see the same issue many times, note it once with an approximate count.

parameters.command:
echo "===LOADAVG==="
cat /proc/loadavg
echo "===CPUCOUNT==="
nproc
echo "===UPTIME==="
uptime -p
echo "===TEMP==="
sensors 2>/dev/null || echo "sensors not available - install lm-sensors and run sensors-detect"
echo "===NIC_STATS==="
ip -s link

messageValues.message:
You are writing a daily health report for a Proxmox VE host, to be read by its administrator over morning coffee. You will be given two things: (1) a list of notable events already extracted from yesterday's system log (possibly gathered from several chunks — merge any obvious duplicates), and (2) a snapshot of current CPU load and physical network interface statistics collected this morning.

Write a concise plain-text report (no markdown, no headers) with this structure:
1. First line: exactly "STATUS: OK" if there is nothing notable in either the log events or the hardware snapshot, or exactly "STATUS: ISSUES" if there is.
2. A 2-4 sentence overview of the day, covering both the log events and anything notable in the hardware snapshot.
3. If STATUS: ISSUES, a bulleted list (using "-") of the specific notable items, grouped by category (errors, security, mail, resources, hardware/CPU, network/NIC, backups), each with a one-line plain-English explanation of what it means and, if obvious, a suggested next step.
4. If STATUS: OK, keep the whole report to 2-3 sentences total and skip the bulleted list.

For the hardware snapshot specifically, only call it out as notable if: 5-minute load average per CPU thread is above roughly 1.0 (sustained high load), any temperature reading is above roughly 80C, or any network interface shows a nonzero error or dropped-packet count, or an interface is DOWN. Otherwise treat the hardware snapshot as healthy and do not mention it in detail.

Keep the total report under 280 words. Be direct and specific — name services, error codes, interface names, or temperatures where present. Do not invent events that are not in the input.
